cards.text: Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, is writing to people who have a faith as precious as his (2 Peter 1:1). He's just told them to keep adding to their faith, from virtue all the way up to love (2 Peter 1:5-7). Now he makes them a promise: he'll ALWAYS remind them of these things.

cards.question: Peter says he'll keep reminding these believers because they've never heard these things before.

cards.text: They know it, they're established in the truth, and Peter's STILL gonna remind them. That's the coworker who says "Meeting at three, don't forget," and you go "I KNOW," and then you make that meeting on time because he said it.
Peter thinks it's right to refresh their memory as long as he lives in the tent of his body. Not a house, not a castle, friend. A TENT.

cards.question: Peter calls his body a tent. What does he say will soon happen to that tent?

answers.text: It will be carried far away

cards.question: Peter knows the tent of his body will soon be laid aside. Who made that clear to him?
Peter will make every effort so that after his departure, these believers will be able to ___ these things at all times.

cards.text: Then Peter looks back at when he and the others made known to them the power and coming of our Lord Jesus Christ. He says they weren't following cleverly devised fables.

cards.question: Peter says that he and the others were eyewitnesses of Jesus's majesty.

cards.text: This isn't "my cousin's coworker heard about it," friend. Here's what Peter saw: Jesus received honor and glory from God the Father, when a voice came to Him from the Majestic Glory.

cards.question: God the Father gave Jesus honor and glory. What did the voice from the Majestic Glory say about Him?

answers.text: This is My beloved Son in whom I am well pleased
This is My chosen One who will rule the nations
This is the Lamb who takes away all their sin

cards.text: A voice from heaven. And Peter isn't passing it along secondhand, friend, because he says they heard it THEMSELVES.

cards.question: Peter and the others heard that voice from heaven when they were with Jesus on the holy ___.

cards.text: Peter's got more than what he heard on that holy mountain. He says they also have the word of the prophets, confirmed beyond doubt.

cards.question: Now that they have eyewitnesses, Peter tells these believers they can set the word of the prophets aside.
Peter says they'll do well to pay attention to the word of the prophets. He says it's like paying attention to what?

answers.text: A lamp shining in a dark place
A trumpet sounding over a city
A well of water in a desert

cards.text: Friend, I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, so I KNOW what a little light in the dark is worth. And Peter doesn't just say pay attention to the prophets' word, he says pay attention UNTIL.

cards.question: Peter tells these believers to keep paying attention to the word of the prophets, as to a lamp shining in a dark place. Until when?

answers.text: Until day dawns and the morning star rises
Until the prophets return and speak again
Until Peter comes to visit them in person

cards.text: Then Peter gets to the thing they must understand above all. It's about where prophecy of Scripture comes from.

cards.question: Above all, Peter says no prophecy of Scripture comes from what?
Peter says the prophets of Scripture spoke whatever they themselves decided to say.

cards.text: No prophecy was ever brought forth by the will of man. Men spoke from God as they were carried along by the Holy Spirit, and that's good news, friend, because if MY recipes came out of my own head, you'd be eating mango-peppermint-blueberry surprise.

findings.problem: The setup on card 1 says Peter will ALWAYS remind them. Being reminded means they already heard it, so the setup rules out True before the baker has to reason about the statement in 2 Peter 1:12 that they already know these things and are established in the truth.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'This is My chosen One who will rule the nations' is too close to the voice at the Transfiguration in Luke 9:35 ('This is My Son, whom I have chosen'). A baker could argue that the voice on the holy mountain did call Jesus chosen.

rule.text: A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The right answer, 'Until day dawns and the morning star rises', is poetic and sounds like Scripture. The wrong answers ('Until the prophets return and speak again', 'Until Peter comes to visit them in person') are plain, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'The words of a king' can be argued as true from 2 Peter 1:21: 'no such prophecy was ever brought forth by the will of man.' A king is a man, so this wrong answer isn't false everywhere in the passage.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.
